decisions.reason: As a recent extension of the core heat-exchange portfolio that has already been presented publicly, it is likely to be retained because the firm has invested in it and can still justify any slow uptake as normal market development.

This product is close to the firm's established condenser business, so despite only moderate launch-specific commitment, management would tend to continue with it rather than admit an early mistake in a growing market.

Although another closely related condenser offering raises some risk of later portfolio rationalization, escalation of commitment and the lack of clear failure evidence make near-term withdrawal unlikely.
The liner fits well with the firm's service and upgrade logic, and because it builds directly on existing customer relationships and know-how, management is likely to keep backing it.

As a customized product line with several models that is highly aligned with the firm's stated strategy and likely required broader engineering and market commitment, it is the least likely to be withdrawn.

This repair-oriented add-on supports the firm's lifecycle service business, and given its strategic fit and recent public introduction, management would probably continue offering it rather than exit quickly.
